 Kentucky head coach Mark Pope understands the Kentucky-Indiana rivalry in basketball because he played in it. And his memories are good ones. On Wednesday at his weekly press conference, he was asked if he had specific memories of playing against the Hoosiers.
 “Yeah. I do. We won both of them,” Pope said. “And I think the year I redshirt, I think we lost. But I remember the divide has been so fun. You think about those games that we used to have in the RCA Dome where half the dome was blue and white, and literally you look down the aisle way, and half the dome was red and white. There’s great history there, and that’s why it’s a special game.”
 Pope believes that this game not only benefits both programs and both fan bases, but the college game as a whole.
 “I think these games are good for college basketball,” Pope said. “They’re good for fan bases. They’re good for just the nature of the game. We love them.”
 Kentucky is 4-1 this season after beating Grambling State 88-59 on Monday night at Rupp Arena. Sophomore center Malachi Moreno had his best game as a Cat, scoring a career-high 22 points and grabbing a career-high 12 rebounds. Zoom Diallo came within a whisker of a triple-double, with 12 points, nine rebounds and nine assists.
 Now, UK turns its attention to Indiana, a team that is 5-0 so far this season. That includes an impressive, neutral site win over No. 20 Arkansas on Tuesday night. Pope knows that the Hoosiers will pose a challenge to his Cats.
 “We have, literally and figuratively, a big test against Indiana coming up with a massive front line, coming off a terrific win,” Pope said. “They’re playing good basketball right now. Darian (DeVries) doing a great job with them. So we’re excited about that game. This Indiana-Kentucky matchup is one of the special ones in sports we’re excited about it.”
 -->
 Wildcats Surge Past Grambling State 
 • Kentucky outscored Grambling State 52-29 in the second half to run away with a 88-59 victory over the Tigers
• Kentucky won the rebounding 49-33, a season-best +16 margin on the glass while also posting a season-best 15 offensive rebounds
• UK had a season-high 22 assists. The Cats have had 20 or more assists in three of their first five games
• Kentucky connected on 10 3-pointers. UK is averaging 9.4 made 3s per game on the season, which would rank fifth in program history for a single season
• Malachi Moreno had a career-night, setting new career highs in points (22) and rebounds (12), while matching his career best with four steals
• Moreno is the first Kentucky player to have at least 22 points, 12 rebounds, four steals and three blocks in a single game and the first SEC player to assemble that stat line since LSU’s Ben Simmons vs. North Florida on Dec. 2, 2015
• Zoom Diallo finished with a near triple-double, totaling 12 points, nine rebounds and nine assists. The nine rebounds were a career-high
 -->
 Diallo’s Shooting is Zooming 
 • Zoom Diallo leads Kentucky in scoring at 14.2 points per game but perhaps even more impressive is how he is doing it
• Diallo is shooting 60.0 percent from the field, including 42.9 percent on 3-pointers, excellent figures for any player, but even more so for a guard
• Diallo, a transfer from Washington, has scored in double figures in four of UK’s first five games, topped by a 24-point outing vs. Kansas
• He came within one rebound and one assist of posting the fifth triple-double in UK history with his 12 points, nine rebounds and nine assists against Grambling State
